Shared native matching and candidate queries
===========================================

native_unify computes a first-order unifier with occurs checking. It reads an
immutable term graph, scoped variable table and initial environment, and writes
a private result environment. The caller publishes that result only on FIRED.
This component is shared machinery for the transform engine and MeTTa matching;
list-rest policies, answer enumeration and host commit are additional components.

Program and execution
---------------------
unify.metta authors one t-ISA p1 program. Its generated text runs through the
independent p1 reference evaluator or the existing x86 emitter. No new t-ISA
instruction is introduced. Native execution is functional evidence; formal
qualification is recorded separately.

The production library executes linked native images. Its admission and ABI
checks do not interpret t-ISA instructions. Reference and comparison execution
are development-only: make check builds a separate library with
DEVELOPMENT_REFERENCE=1. native_match.h retains the development operation codes
for those checks; production rejects them. nm_unify_program_default loads the embedded reference text and
calls the prelinked image, with no file, code generation or executable mapping.
The file-loading development entrypoint also emits comparison bytes and
requires them to equal the linked image. Comparison mode runs isolated region
copies, checks all bytes and boundary guards, and publishes agreed private work
only after agreement. nm_unify_call distinguishes invalid host arguments,
allocation failure and differential disagreement from declared machine
outcomes. The packaged sources build as ordinary C and assembly; regenerating
them uses export.py and the MeTTa author.

native_unify.S contains a four-byte indirect-branch landing pad followed by
the exact p1 image, a read-only byte copy and the reference program text.
Registration checks the entry and image bytes before native execution.
test_linked.py checks the actual linked code and embedded model, and verifies
rejection of changed landing-pad and body bytes. This is byte qualification,
not a formal refinement theorem for either the image or the landing pad.

The public arguments are the two root node ids. Node zero is reserved as the
unbound-environment value and cannot occur as a root or child.

Region  Access  Representation
0       RO      four-word nodes: kind, a, b, c
1       RO      child node ids, one word each
2       RO      initial environment: node id or zero, one word per variable
3       RW      private result environment, at least as large as region 2
4       RW      pending pairs, two words per entry, at least one entry
5       RW      occurs-check worklist, one word per entry, at least one entry
6       RO      variable keys, two words per variable: variable id, scope id
7       RW      private controller state, 40 words
8       RW      variable/node epoch marks, then the rigid-pair memo table

All regions have eight-byte alignment. The standard p1 entry contract supplies
their extents and separation. Only complete node/edge/worklist entries are
used. The environment and variable-key vectors must have the stated exact
relationship. All capacities are explicit; the component allocates no memory.

Nodes
-----
kind 0: a is an opaque constant's semantic identity; b and c are zero.
kind 1: a is the variable's dense slot; (b,c) equals its (variable id,scope id)
        entry in region 6.
kind 2: a is the first child position; b is the number of children; c is zero.
        Every child id is positive and earlier than this node's id.

Variable keys are strictly ordered by (scope id,variable id), so a key cannot
be assigned two distinct slots. Distinct nodes may denote the same term or
variable. Equality is semantic; node identity is only an equality shortcut.
The host adapter supplies semantic identities for opaque constants and retains
the original values and their owners for projecting returned node ids.

Region 8 holds variables+nodes epoch-mark words followed by a positive,
power-of-two number of memo slots. Every word is cleared before use. Occurs
checking visits each shared node once per scan. A memo entry packs two positive
32-bit tuple node ids into one word; zero means empty. Recording a pair means
its child constraints have been scheduled. Binding only adds constraints, so
another occurrence of that pair does not schedule them again. The memo is
private to one unification attempt and never reused across calls.

The component validates node shape, child bounds, variable keys and initial
bindings. Occurs checking also rejects cyclic initial environments. Both input
sides may contain variables. A fresh schema import receives fresh scope ids;
shared state variables retain their scope ids.

Outcomes
--------
FIRED (1): region 3 holds the resulting environment; payload is the number of
new bindings written during this call.
REFUSED (0): the terms have no unifier; payload zero. Inputs are unchanged and
the private result is discarded.
UNSUPPORTED (2): malformed representation, insufficient private capacity or an
iteration cap; payload identifies the cause. Inputs are unchanged; private
work is discarded.
INVALID (3): the standard p1 entry/access checks reject the physical call.
EXHAUSTED (4): a FUND point cannot be paid. The exact p1 receipt is retained.

The current p1 authoring profile admits explicit RETURN codes 0,1,2 only.
Representation faults therefore use UNSUPPORTED with a distinct reason;
they never masquerade as no unifier. Higher-level adapters retain that cause.

Reason codes
------------
1 bad vector layout or loop bound; 2 invalid root/node id; 3 malformed node;
4 invalid variable key; 5 invalid/cyclic initial environment;
6 insufficient result/mark capacity; 7 pending-pair capacity;
8 occurs-worklist capacity; 9 iteration cap; 10 rigid-pair memo capacity.

Fuel
----
One unit per transition of the bounded work loop. Its declared phases perform
one variable initialization/key check, node or child validation, environment
validation request, dereference, pair selection, pair comparison, occurs-check
node or child push. Phase completion and continuation transitions also pay one
unit. The fixed physical-layout checks precede the loop. The whole loop has a
2^32-1 transition cap. Workspace writes are private to the call; the caller
publishes the result only after FIRED.

Constraint truth
----------------
For this finite first-order component, a successful call with zero new
bindings means the tested constraint already holds under the initial
substitution. Success with new bindings instead supplies a possible extension:
it does not establish a guard under the initial context. A refused call means
no finite unifier exists. nm_constraint_truth exposes ENTAILED, OPEN and
REFUTED accordingly. Exhaustion, unsupported inputs, invalid physical calls
and host failures supply no logical verdict; their original causes remain
available. A stable equality guard accepts only ENTAILED. Matching or a tell
may extend the context with an OPEN result after its ordinary admission.
This is executable component semantics; its machine-code proof remains open.

Native template instantiation
-----------------------------
emit.metta authors a second t-ISA p1 component over the same first-order graph
and scoped key representation. native_emit.h exposes its prelinked x86 image,
reference execution and isolated comparison through the shared private runner
in native_component.c. Recovering the matcher through that runner leaves its
program text and exact bytes unchanged. Exporting a component supplies no
machine-code proof; native_emit.hol records the image for later qualification.

The emitter follows transitive bindings, rejects reachable cycles, preserves
unbound scoped keys and constructs an immutable postorder output DAG. It does
not rename free variables or evaluate a term. One source memo and one variable
memo span the entire bundle. This avoids repeated expansion across roots while
retaining repeated root occurrences. Memos are private to one fixed context;
distinct answer contexts are never merged by sharing a constructed graph.

Region  Access  Representation
0       RO      input nodes, four words each
1       RO      input child ids
2       RO      fixed variable bindings
3       RW      output nodes, five words: kind, a, b, c, source-node label
4       RW      output child ids
5       RW      source-node and variable memo words
6       RW      explicit DFS frames, four words each
7       RW      controller state, 40 words
8       RO      variable keys, two words each

Arg0 is the source root. Arg1 is the declared output-node capacity. A bundle
is represented by a synthetic tuple root. The caller supplies all workspace;
node zero is reserved. Every output child id precedes its parent. Output nodes
retain the source label for ownership/provenance transport; that label is not
an already-instantiated host value. The generated state coordinates come from
emit_layout.metta; C checks its actual node/frame layouts at compile time.

The FIRED payload is the output root id. UNSUPPORTED retains a separate cause:
1 layout, 2 root/binding id, 3 shape/key/child, 4 node capacity, 5 edge capacity,
6 memo capacity, 7 DFS capacity, 8 binding cycle, 9 transition cap. EXHAUSTED and
INVALID remain distinct outcomes. One fuel unit is charged per work transition;
private prefix counts and consumed fuel are retained on supported failure exits.
No partial output may be published.

native_output.h packages import, private allocation and native construction
for host templates. nm_output_build accepts a stable term view, including an
immutable solution view, and returns an owned immutable materialized bundle.
It charges one activation before import plus the component's fuel. Import
callback limits are separate from machine fuel. Outputs include repeated root
ids and full variable/scope identities. Source owners and the pin token remain
borrowed; source callbacks are not invoked after construction. The callback
context, solution snapshot and program may be released after the call.

Only a completed build with a valid pin yields a graph. Incomplete work, stale
views, unsupported source values and provider faults stay distinct. Accessors
recheck the pin; a host still validates its commit token before publication.
This operation does not perform a host-store commit, generative schema
freshening, or AnswerSpace collection. A materialized bundle alone is not the
complete answer context or evidence that a query has finished.

Contextual import and projection
--------------------------------
native_match_view.h imports a stable host view into the native graph. Host
values are an opaque pair (syntax, context). The adapter never evaluates them
and never erases their lexical or ownership context. Callbacks supply node
shape, children and initial variable bindings. Constant identities must be
reflexive equality classes; a different matching policy must return DEFER.

An iterative postorder traversal assigns owned graph ids, without assuming
anything about host id order. Value and variable maps preserve sharing and
scoped variable identities. The importer rejects raw source cycles as DEFER;
cyclic initial substitutions are subsequently rejected by native validation.
Limits count nodes, edges, variables and callback invocations. Interrupted
reads, unsupported shape/policy, resource exhaustion and provider faults are
distinct. Source owners and pinned views remain borrowed through projection.

nm_match_prepare_constraints conjoins several equations in one private
unification attempt, with two synthetic tuple roots. Every equation shares
the same substitution. Empty conjunctions are supported. Synthetic roots
count against capacity and cannot be projected as source values.

After success, nm_match_project returns the original variable and its binding
value, their contexts, their scoped key and whether the binding is new.
Projection neither creates host syntax nor publishes a binding. Existing
bindings cannot be rewritten through this projection.

nm_solution_capture copies a successful projection into an immutable private
read view. It can outlive the original native graph and workspace; the host
syntax owners and external source-view context remain borrowed. A parent
solution is retained automatically. New refinements shadow their parents,
with iterative lookup and release. Entry count and chain depth are observable.
Capture also checks that the number of newly bound slots agrees with the
unifier's payload. nm_solution_visit_changes exposes only introduced bindings,
with their full scoped keys and original value contexts, newest refinement
first. It preserves valid zero-valued host encodings. The visitor supplies data
for the host's grouped publication protocol; it does not implement that protocol.
The snapshot does not publish to the host. A later guard can query this view
without assuming an open constraint or changing the earlier branch: X=a is
OPEN before the tell, ENTAILED after it; X=b is then REFUTED for distinct a,b.

Equational admission
--------------------
native_admission.h composes the equational fragment after premise matching.
Tells extend a private solution context. Equality guards accept only ENTAILED;
OPEN guards stop without being assumed. The declared ask policy runs guards
before all tells or after all tells. Contradictory tells, open guards, refuted
guards and operational failures remain distinguishable.

The controller is C orchestration over the shared native/reference query and
unifier implementations. It does not introduce another solver. Each activated
equation pays one fuel unit in addition to the unifier's exact receipt. A next
call's quantum bounds equation activations. Failed calls retain fuel spent,
completed tell/guard counts, snapshots, peak refinement depth and query-work
statistics. Traces identify the clause and preserve the underlying events.

Only ADMITTED exposes a final context; taking the result transfers its owned
reference. The input context is unchanged on every path. Source syntax owners
and view contexts remain borrowed, and the host must revalidate its own commit
token before publication. This component has equality guards only. Region
guards use the census component; output-row construction and host commit follow.

Complete region observations
-----------------------------
native_census.h supplies absence, exact-count and stable-region observations
under a fixed first-order context. It uses the same matcher to classify each
row as certain (already equal) or possible (unifiable after an extension).
Occurrence multiplicity is retained. It validates the pattern and reachable
initial substitution before scanning, including for an empty region.

An observation is available only after a complete scan while the pinned view
is valid. Absence requires zero possible rows; a stable count requires exactly
the target number of certain rows and no additional possible ones. A stable
region likewise has certain == possible. NOT_ENTAILED is not a proof of the
underlying proposition's negation. An unfinished or failed scan supplies no
guard verdict, even when its partial counts are zero.

Validation and scan work have separate counters and share a cumulative fuel
receipt. Traces tag validation versus row probes and retain the last row,
outcome and cause. The controller performs C orchestration over the native
query/unifier; it does not add another matcher. Connecting region checks into
an ordered full firing protocol remains integration work.

Finite candidate queries
------------------------
native_query.h enumerates ordered selections from a pinned, finite row view.
Rows have unique occurrence ids; equal terms at different occurrences remain
separate candidates. The first `takes` premises require distinct occurrences.
Reads may repeat other reads but cannot select a taken occurrence. This is a
positive first-order query component, before symmetry quotienting, guards,
semantic scheduling and commit.

Reference mode uses C advancement/exclusivity and p1 reference unification.
Native mode uses the two private x86 routines in native_selection.S and the
linked unifier. Comparison mode checks advancement, exclusivity and all
unifier results and regions against the reference implementations. The two
selection routines use the ordinary SysV ABI and indirect-branch landing
pads. Registration checks their bytes against read-only copies; linked-image
tests also compare them with the object. Their machine-code proofs remain
open independently of their executable tests.

One next-call quantum bounds complete candidate proposals. YIELD retains the
cursor for another call. END, EXHAUSTED, DEFER, RESOURCE, INTERRUPTED,
INVALIDATED and FAULT remain distinct; none of the latter mean an empty
answer set. Native fuel is a cumulative unifier-transition receipt, separate
from proposals and import callbacks. It is not a bound on total CPU work.

Answers borrow the selected occurrences, prepared graph and private result
through the next call or query release. The source is never mutated. Optional
trace callbacks observe proposals, imports and core outcomes, including exact
receipts. Pinned-view callbacks enforce validity before dereferencing source
storage; the query additionally checks validity before returning an answer.

The current candidate search is a Cartesian baseline. Indexed joins, source
representation reuse and pattern specialization remain performance work; no
speedup is established. Stored rows retain the variable interpretation of
their supplied host values. Per-use schematic-row instantiation is additional
machinery, not an implicit change of scope.

Optional tcalc term client
-------------------------
native_tcalc_view.h adapts CeTTa's first-order TcTerms through public accessors.
Locals use the supplied activation context; state unknowns use the fixed state
scope. A live high-water id and stable table are supplied by the table owner.
The view has an empty external substitution. Publishing a state still needs
tcalc's closing operation for unbound locals.

`make check-tcalc CETTA=<checkout>` compares native/reference/compare decisions
and ground results against the actual, unmodified tcalc C solver. It does not
install a CeTTa runtime hook or qualify complete transform firings. The
standalone library has no CeTTa build dependency.

Remaining native coverage
-------------------------
This first component does not complete a general MeTTa matcher or tcalc engine.
Remaining components include concrete runtime custody, list rests
and grounded comparison policy, binding publication/retention, indexed joins
and schematic-row enumeration, full ordered guard/transform admission
and commit under every declared interpretation. The standalone and CeTTa routes
must ultimately call the same implementations and share their conformance corpus.
